reviews.snippet:
My husband and I visited Aster Whitefield on June 6 for an orthopaedic consultation, and unfortunately, our experience was extremely disappointing.

From the moment we arrived, there was no one available to guide or assist patients, making the entire process confusing and unorganized.

The consultation itself was even more concerning. Instead of taking the time to explain the diagnosis, discuss treatment options, and outline the pros and cons of both conservative management and surgery, the doctor immediately suggested surgery as the primary solution. The way this was communicated was alarming and left us feeling frightened, anxious, and overwhelmed.

Healthcare professionals should understand that patients visit hospitals seeking reassurance, clarity, and compassionate guidance during difficult times. Presenting surgery as the first and only option without adequate explanation or empathy can have a significant impact on a patient’s mental well-being. We left the hospital feeling far more distressed than when we arrived, and the anxiety stayed with us long after the consultation.

Based on our experience, I believe the hospital needs to improve both its patient support services and the communication skills of its medical staff. Patients deserve to be treated with empathy, respect, and clear information so they can make informed decisions about their health.

Unfortunately, our experience was so negative that I would not recommend Aster Whitefield to others.

response.snippet:
Namaste Rach,

We sincerely regret to hear about your experience and understand your disappointment regarding the consultation, communication, and overall patie

Doctor explained all the procedure clearly, Dr is very humble with patients and treatment was superb. Nursing staffs are well trained and very friendlyI.Nurse Yasmeen baig patient care was very good. She has good knowledge and communication. We strongly recommend Aster hospital for their patient care.

Feedback to Aster Hospitals – Whitefield

I would like to share my recent experience at Aster Hospitals. First, I want to sincerely appreciate the excellent team of doctors and nurses you have. Their dedication and care are commendable, and I am truly grateful for their service.

On 23rd January, I underwent a DJ stent removal surgery with Dr. Santhosh. He is one of the finest doctors I have ever met—professional, compassionate, and highly skilled. My experience with him and the nursing staff was outstanding. For example, when the nurse call button in the day care room was not working, the sisters responded politely and assured me that it would be fixed. Their attitude reflected genuine care for patients.

However, I regret to say that my experience with hospital management was disappointing, particularly with Ms. Rashmi. During discharge, I requested a water mug, only to learn that it had been missing from the washroom for at least a week. When I raised this concern, Ms. Rashmi responded dismissively, saying, “I am not the one who comes to your washroom and checks it.”

As a patient, I believe it is my right to question such lapses, especially in a branded hospital that charges fixed and premium prices. Instead of addressing the issue professionally, her response came across as argumentative and dismissive. This reflects poorly on the hospital’s management, even though the medical and nursing services are excellent.

To be clear, my disappointment is not with the doctors or nurses, who are exceptional, but with the management staff who failed to uphold the standards expected from a reputed institution like Aster.

My name is Umamaheswara Reddy, and you may verify my case with Aster Whitefield Hospital if needed. I am sharing this feedback not to criticize unnecessarily, but to highlight areas where improvement is essential. Patients deserve not only excellent medical care but also respectful and responsible management.

Worst pediatrics department. For our 10 year old daughter who just had a stomach infection they were ready to do appendicitis surgery. After repeated ultrasound and blood reports also they were not satisfied and wanted us to get admitted for a CT scan and later were planning for surgery among themselves. No attention on the so young patient who was so panicked by hearing them(though she is such a strong girl). They Just want money. Horrible experience. I request all to get a second opinion whenever you go there and get a suggestion for surgery. I don't want to take name of the money minded pediatric  surgeon. She will surely understand whom I am talking about. Please don't go there if you love your child. Our child is absolutely fine after referring other pediatrician.

Please avoid this branch of Aster. Kindly go to CMI or RV. The staff here is severely undertrained and unaware of processes. Lack of structure and service will be noticed within 10 mins of stepping in the Hospital. Asked me to pay 1.25 lakhs for my mother’s hospitalisation for 3 days in general ward, though there is no surgery involved; only for health management. Living in 5star hotel is cheaper than this. To top that off they weren’t willing to give me a breakup for the verbal estimation given. The co ordinator kept insisting that there is no fixed pricing.
Don’t even have helping staff to push the wheelchair, you will have to do it yourself. Their management should go to Kochi Aster and take notes.Seriously surprised how this can come under the Aster brand! Terrible experience and waste of money.

Horrible Hospital for In-pateints, For OPD it is fine, For any Surgery or want to admit here.. Don't even consider this, The service provided here is equivalent to General ward of Govt Hospital.

They Have Good Infrastructure & Hired best Doctors & managing with that, they don't have systems in place, very poor coordination, no body takes responsibilities except docters.

What i understood is the top management don't see this as a health care or a service, They are just doing business.

Fraudulent  activities by insurance team / hospital team by merging with insurance agents to cheat patients

I had very bad experience in the aster hospital white feild.

We have under gone day care procedure for spinal injection for leg pain

Before the surgery we have told the hospital team if our insurance is approved only we will come for procedure.

Then started the drama

.... before the surgery insurance team has applied for pre approval...and got pre approved without mentioning exact procedural details and asked us to come for procedure..

after the procedure they have shared the procedure details mentioning it is for injection...then insurance department had been rejected the approval provided prior..
When we contacted the insurance department they have mentioned that the injection procedure is not covered under your plan which is not mentioned during pre approval

When we contact the billing team...they told that is insurance responsibility we are no where responsible for this rejection

Rated 1 because the day 1 experience is very bad. My father and husband are not allowed inside as my mom is in ICU and room charges are taken for 6 days where the room is also not allotted because patient is in ICU. No one should be there with patient , and even when asked about food yes you can bring from home. They came back to bring food and later they were denied entry. The worst management and the worst rooms I have seen. Because firstly they shifted to room than the AC had a leakage, they changed room and finally denied. My stuff is there and the room is allotted to someone else. My moms knee surgery I would have planned somewhere with better management. Do not go for any surgeries here, until and unless they have a management who can look after patient and concern of family. Manipal Hospital is much better I regret my decision now to come to Aster.

The service level needs to seriously improve by a lot . I have admitted my father for basilic vein superfisialization . He was admitted and after surgery and dialysis , when he was supposed to be shifted to in room . It took 2 Hrs to connect with the in room support and dialysis team within the same premises to arrange for shifting after several followups , which the patient family had to do . The response from the hospital staff was we have informed the in room team and they will do it the shifting . Not only that , the next day the doctor did the review and approved release process at 10.30am , and the in house team till 5pm kept saying we have not got the release details , billing team billed extra for no fault of patient . This was finally resolved after multiple communications and after escalating to the Aster WF Head of Operations . Patient Name Amal Kumar Dey a CKD patient of 83 Yrs had to go thru this . Hope the management listens to patients grievances and make the changes Thanks Tanmoy

I had a very bad experience with the hospital. I don't know how many others have faced this, but I can assure you that I've seen several cases similar to mine. We planned the surgery nearly two weeks in advance, scheduled an appointment with the doctor, and confirmed that everything was organized. We informed them well ahead of time that we needed a single room, considering we have small children to care for.

However, upon arrival, we were told that a single room was not available and were asked to admit ourselves to the general ward, with the assurance that we would be moved as soon as a room opened up in the evening. The frustrating part is that we planned carefully, and they were aware they didn’t have a room available. Yet, they still called us, expecting us to accommodate this disorganized and unprofessional experience. I saw a couple of others in the same situation that day who reluctantly agreed, but I refused.
No care once you get admitted. One nurse assigned for each floor. Duty doc visits an Hr later once request is made. I am talking about with patient with surgery and private room.

This review is regarding a small surgery done in Aster hospital.. the Issue was with Fissure and piles. Hence we were suggested a small surgery using laser in the Rectal area.. we were told that the patient will get admitted in the morning and the next day the patient will be discharged. We followed all protocols provided by Dr Prabhakar and the hospital and got the patient admitted. They performed the surgery and informed us that everything is fine. However, right the next day, patient started getting fever with low oxygen level. Instead of getting discharged the next day, the patient had to stay in the hospital for another 2 days tolerating heavy medication. The patient was having immense pain and none of the pain killers worked. We were informed that the pain is common and will go away after 1 week. They discharged the patient with the pain. After getting the patient home, she was suffering like hell. Hence we took the patient back to emergency again. This time, the doctor suggested another surgery and had to pay another heavy bill. Even this time, the patient was kept admitted for 2 days. She was still having the same pain.. since there was no improvement at all even after 2 surgeries, we stopped visiting Aster and took the patient to a different hospital. Now she is recovering but as informed, the operation wasn’t successful at all. I am giving one star just cz they were unable to do correct treatment.

While the doctors were excellent, the hospital administration was among the worst we've encountered. During our two-day post-surgery stay, we had a very bad experience. Patient food was never delivered on time, requiring numerous follow-ups. The nurses were very laid back and uncaring, expecting us to administer medicines and monitor the IV ourselves. Bed sheets were not changed on time and required constant reminders. The discharge process was particularly frustrating; initiated at 8 am, we didn't receive the discharge until 7 pm, with no regular updates from the staff. They refused to provide a copy of the bill until full payment was made, displaying a deplorable attitude. Very poor coordination and overall not worth the money they are charging.

Try to avoid this hospital...and search for a better options if not dazzled by the glitters and glasses.
Only the infrastructure they maintain from outside looks good, rest other things like patient care , hygiene and emergency support is lower than the worst.
My mother underwent an abdominal surgery there. The nurses never respond on time and they don't really care about the patient need after surgery, you will be left in the room unattended even after pressing multiple alarms. Never ever get admitted on Sunday's , it turns into a ghost zone, you won't find any nurses or helping boy on Sunday's , and ultimately have to starve to death .
It's more a corporate organization than a hospital.
Also their insurance department is at other level to torture you more. The insurance company never approves their claim as they always quote the triple amount.

Only positive is the doctor's kind and understanding behavior and making patient comfortable.

Pathetic experience. There is no queue management here. Don’t even have sitting capacity for waiting patients. My father aged 65 with spine surgery had to stand for 15 mins to get a chair to seat. No display system for queued patients. You don’t know when your turn will come. You have to indefinitely wait. If you go to rest room and you miss your turn you don’t know when you will be called back. They have just hired some good doctors from other hospitals which forces patients to visit this hospital. After all now a days patient word is becoming useless. Its customers and hospital.

Our Family’s Experience

We had our first baby at this hospital. Like any other family, we researched thoroughly to find the best hospital, and this seemed to be the one. Dr. Kavita Kovi came highly recommended; many people spoke well of her, and at first, we trusted her. However, just before the delivery, she informed us that our baby had obstructive hydrocephalus, caused by toxoplasma in the mother's body.

My question is, why didn’t the radiology department catch this earlier? It's impossible for toxoplasma to develop in just two days. At the last moment, Dr. Kavita advised an emergency C-section due to the severity of the situation.

After our baby was born, we encountered the same situation many parents seem to face – the baby was placed in the NICU due to difficulty breathing. Of course, we trusted the hospital’s decisions, assuming they knew what was best for our baby.

Then came Dr. Lathish. He excels at speaking rudely to parents and instilling panic. More than that, he seems intent on inflating hospital bills and complicating matters. We faced so many problems, and we were put in a position where we felt trapped, unable to go anywhere else.

Our nephew had to undergo brain surgery, which led to complications and infections. It became painfully clear that these doctors didn’t actually care about their patients, and I can’t understand how people in such a profession could act this way.

After we complained about Dr. Lathish’s behavior, we were directed to Dr. Srinivas by the higher authorities. He is skilled at downplaying serious issues, brushing everything off as "common" and offering the same vague reassurance for every concern. He never addressed our baby's actual condition, leaving us feeling helpless.

This hospital lacks basic humanity; it is entirely focused on business. Tragically, we lost our nephew. We’ve researched and continue to search for answers about what went wrong. But nothing can change the fact that our baby is no longer with us.

Thank you, doctors, for doing what you did. I know you don’t care because you’ve already gotten what you needed—money. The pain and loss we are enduring is ours alone to bear. My only hope is that no one else has to go through what we did.

I urge everyone reading this to be vigilant. Don’t neglect any detail, and please, avoid this place. We miss our baby terribly, and I can’t help but think that if we had never come here, our baby might still be with us.

Patient service was horrible the day of admission. It took 2 hours for nurse to decide what they should do. Post surgery nurses are running around and when asked we are shortstaffed. The time doctor said discharge was 11am but you get out of the hospital is at 8pm. 4 hours of nursing to complete there activity and 3 hours for billing to complete. The insurance cleared it in 30 mins. I had gone along with my father who is 78yrs. The worst patient service I have ever faced in Bangalore.

I'm writing here to ensure that nobody else faces the same issue.

My daughter, who is 1.6 years old, fell from a bike and sustained a minor scalp injury. Despite eight months of treatment, the wound has not fully healed. We sought a second opinion from plastic surgeons at Aster Hospital. Initially, the treatment was progressing well under the care of a competent doctor. However, the situation worsened when a staff member named ( NIDA-Plastic Surgery department ) intervened. She prematurely removed the scab, causing the wound to regress to its initial state. This setback required us to visit the hospital daily for three weeks to clean the wound. Subsequent treatment from another staff member showed improvement, but due to Nida's absence, we were forced to return to her for wound care. Unfortunately, her intervention led to the wound reverting to its original condition.

My sincere request to the management is to refrain from allowing individuals to experiment and test things in sensitive situations like this. I urge for appropriate action to be taken against this lady( NIDA-Plastic Surgery department ) to prevent similar incidents from occurring to others

I was not only mistreated in this hospital, I was ripped off a lot of money. Dr Somshekar made me run hundreds of tests and right before the day of my surgery he refused to do it because I had complained to the management regarding my mistreatment. He not only suffers from God syndrome but also wasted an entire day ofnmine just to refuse my surgery. Just because he has the power. I had spoken to the managemnet and complained about being mistreated and I got mistreated all the more.

My Father was an International patient, who was undergoing treatment under Professor Dr. Somasekhar SP at Aster Whitefield Hospital. I was very disappointed & deceived by the hospital treatment. My father was going to have pipec surgery but instead, they did a normal test which was not necessary at all & gave us a very expensive bill. He didn't take our permission to do the test instead of surgery & didn't meet with us after the test. Their International Marketing person at Whitefield was not helpful at all. We visited different hospitals after that and got confirmation of being deceived by the hospital authority.
